plan.title: VaultRegistry + File Watcher + IndexQueue + Markdown Parser + NoteTypeClassifier

task.description:
Create server/app/vault/registry.py — VaultRegistry: path-to-owner resolution.
Implementation: - VaultRegistry class with in-memory mapping of vault paths to (user_id, namespace). - Vault structure: /vaults/private/{username}/ and /vaults/shared/. - rebuild(db: AsyncSession) -> None: queries users table, rebuilds path mapping. /vaults/shared/ maps to (SYSTEM_USER_ID, "shared"). /vaults/private/{username}/ maps to (user.id, "private"). - resolve(filepath: str) -> tuple[UUID, str] | None: Match filepath against known vault paths. Return (user_id, namespace) or None if outside all vaults. - PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY integration: On user create/delete, send NOTIFY vault_registry_refresh. Background task listens for vault_registry_refresh and calls rebuild(). - Called on app startup to populate initial mapping.
Thread safety: use threading.Lock for the internal mapping since watchdog events arrive from a background thread.
task.verification: VaultRegistry.resolve("/vaults/private/alice/notes/test.md") returns (alice_user_id, "private"). VaultRegistry.resolve("/vaults/shared/docs/readme.md") returns (SYSTEM_USER_ID, "shared"). VaultRegistry.resolve("/tmp/random.md") returns None. rebuild() populates mapping from users table. LISTEN/NOTIFY trigger is set up.
task.done-condition: VaultRegistry resolves filesystem paths to (user_id, namespace) tuples. Returns None for paths outside known vaults. Rebuilds on startup and on NOTIFY vault_registry_refresh. Thread-safe via Lock.

dimension.name: risk
dimension.rationale: Wrong resolution = wrong user sees wrong data

task.description:
Create server/app/vault/watcher.py — watchdog file watcher with 300ms debounce.
Implementation: - VaultEventHandler(FileSystemEventHandler): watches for .md file create/modify/delete/rename. - Debounce: 300ms (from settings vault.watch_debounce_ms). Use a timer dict keyed by filepath. On event, cancel existing timer for that path and set a new one. - Thread-safe handoff to asyncio: Use loop.call_soon_threadsafe(queue.put_nowait, event) per spec. Get loop via asyncio.get_running_loop() (never get_event_loop). - Event types: ("created", path), ("modified", path), ("deleted", path), ("moved", src, dest). - Filter: only .md files. Ignore hidden files/dirs (starting with .). - start_watcher(vault_base_path, loop, queue) -> Observer: creates and starts watchdog Observer. - stop_watcher(observer) -> None: stops the Observer gracefully.
CRITICAL per spec: use loop.call_soon_threadsafe, NOT asyncio.get_event_loop().
task.verification: VaultEventHandler only processes .md files. Debounce is 300ms. Uses loop.call_soon_threadsafe for thread handoff. Does NOT use asyncio.get_event_loop(). `grep "get_event_loop" server/app/vault/watcher.py` returns no matches. `grep "call_soon_threadsafe" server/app/vault/watcher.py` returns a match.
task.done-condition: watchdog Observer watches vault directories for .md changes. Events are debounced at 300ms. Thread-safe handoff to asyncio via call_soon_threadsafe. Only .md files processed. Hidden files ignored.

dimension.name: testing
dimension.rationale: Create test file, verify event queued

task.description:
Create server/app/vault/indexer.py — IndexQueue: async queue consumer for vault events.
Implementation: - IndexQueue class wrapping asyncio.Queue. - enqueue(event_type: str, filepath: str, user_id: UUID, namespace: str) -> None: add to queue. - process_queue() -> None: async loop that dequeues events and processes them. Phase 1 processing: - For "created"/"modified": read file, compute content_hash. If content_hash unchanged, skip. Otherwise, upsert document record in DB (file_path, content, content_hash, note_type from classifier, frontmatter). Extract wikilinks and upsert into wikilinks table. Log to index_events table. Do NOT embed (Phase 2). - For "deleted": mark document as deleted or remove from DB. Remove associated chunks and wikilinks. - For "moved": update file_path. Update wikilinks that reference old path. - App-initiated writes: skip watcher by matching content_hash (watcher event arrives but content_hash matches, so no re-index). - bulk_index(db, user_id, namespace, vault_path) -> None: walks vault directory, enqueues all .md files. Used on startup for unindexed vaults.
Create server/app/api/vault.py — GET /api/v1/vault/index/progress endpoint. - Returns IndexProgressResponse: { current: int, total: int, eta: str|null, status: "idle"|"indexing"|"complete" } - Requires get_current_user. - Reads progress from IndexQueue state.
Register vault router in server/app/main.py.
task.verification: IndexQueue.enqueue adds events to the async queue. process_queue handles created/modified/deleted/moved events. content_hash skip logic prevents re-indexing unchanged files. `grep "embedding" server/app/vault/indexer.py | grep -v "^#"` returns no matches (Phase 1 must not assign embedding field). GET /api/v1/vault/index/progress returns IndexProgressResponse. `grep "Depends(get_current_user)" server/app/api/vault.py` returns a match. Vault router registered in main.py. Endpoint requires Depends(get_current_user).
task.done-condition: IndexQueue consumes vault events asynchronously. Documents are upserted with content_hash dedup. Wikilinks extracted and stored. Deletions cascade. GET /api/v1/vault/index/progress reports current/total/status. Bulk index walks entire vault directory.

task.description:
Create server/app/vault/parser.py — Markdown frontmatter extraction and wikilink parsing.
Implementation: - parse_markdown(filepath: str) -> ParsedNote: Uses python-frontmatter to extract YAML frontmatter and content body. Returns ParsedNote dataclass: { frontmatter: dict, content: str, title: str, file_path: str } Title: from frontmatter "title" key, or filename without extension. - extract_wikilinks(content: str) -> list[WikilinkRef]: Regex: \[\[([^\]|]+)(?:\|([^\]]+))?\]\] Captures target (group 1) and optional alias (group 2). Returns list of WikilinkRef dataclass: { target: str, alias: str|None } Handles edge cases: nested brackets, escaped brackets, code blocks (skip).
Create server/app/rag/note_type.py — NoteTypeClassifier.
Implementation: - NoteTypeClassifier class. - classify(frontmatter: dict, folder_path: str, tags: list[str]) -> str: Returns one of: "fleeting", "literature", "permanent", "project", "reference", "index". Priority: 1. Explicit frontmatter "type" field → use directly. 2. Folder matching (from settings zettelkasten.note_types): - fleeting_folders → "fleeting" - project_folders → "project" 3. Tag matching: - fleeting_tags → "fleeting" - project_tags → "project" 4. Default: "permanent" (the Zettelkasten atomic note type). - Uses settings from config module for folder/tag patterns.
task.verification: parse_markdown extracts frontmatter dict and content string. extract_wikilinks("See [[Target]] and [[Other|Alias]]") returns [{target: "Target", alias: None}, {target: "Other", alias: "Alias"}]. Wikilinks inside code blocks are NOT extracted. NoteTypeClassifier with frontmatter {"type": "literature"} returns "literature". NoteTypeClassifier with folder "/inbox/test.md" returns "fleeting" (matched by fleeting_folders). Default classification is "permanent".
task.done-condition: Markdown parser extracts frontmatter and wikilinks correctly (including [[Target|Alias]] syntax). Code blocks are skipped during wikilink extraction. NoteTypeClassifier infers type from frontmatter > folder > tags > default("permanent"). Settings-driven folder/tag patterns work. Runnable check: `python -c "from app.vault.parser import extract_wikilinks; result = extract_wikilinks('See [[Target]] and [[Other|Alias]]'); assert len(result) == 2 and result[1].alias == 'Alias'"` exits 0. Runnable check: `python -c "from app.rag.note_type import NoteTypeClassifier; c = NoteTypeClassifier(); assert c.classify({'type': 'literature'}, '', []) == 'literature'"` exits 0. Integration coverage: `pytest server/tests/integration/test_vault.py -k "parser or classifier" -v` exits 0 after PLAN-1-7 is complete.

task.description:
Wire vault subsystem into app startup in server/app/main.py.
Startup sequence additions: 1. Create VaultRegistry instance. Call registry.rebuild(db) on startup. 2. Create asyncio.Queue for vault events. 3. Start IndexQueue consumer as a background task (asyncio.create_task). 4. Start watchdog Observer via start_watcher(settings.vault.base_path, loop, queue). 5. Set up LISTEN/NOTIFY listener for vault_registry_refresh.
Shutdown sequence: 1. Stop watchdog Observer. 2. Cancel IndexQueue consumer task. 3. Close LISTEN/NOTIFY connection.
Register vault_registry as app state (app.state.vault_registry) for access in route handlers.
task.verification: App startup creates VaultRegistry, starts watcher, starts IndexQueue consumer. App shutdown stops watcher and cancels consumer. VaultRegistry is accessible via app.state.vault_registry. Uses asyncio.get_running_loop() (not get_event_loop).
task.done-condition: Application startup initializes VaultRegistry (rebuild from DB), starts watchdog Observer on vault base path, starts IndexQueue consumer as background task, and sets up LISTEN/NOTIFY. Shutdown gracefully stops all three. VaultRegistry accessible from route handlers via app.state.

plan.dependencies: PLAN-1-6 depends on PLAN-1-3 (needs Document, Chunk, Wikilink models + DB session) and PLAN-1-4 (needs get_current_user for vault API endpoint)

decision.choice: Used asyncio.ensure_future(registry.rebuild_bg(), loop=loop) inside the asyncpg listener callback instead of loop.call_soon_threadsafe with a create_task wrapper
decision.rationale: asyncpg listener callbacks run on the asyncio event loop thread, so ensure_future is safe and avoids the complexity of a threadsafe wrapper. The loop reference captured in the closure is the same running loop as the one used throughout the lifespan.
decision.alternatives-considered: loop.call_soon_threadsafe(asyncio.create_task, ...) — rejected because create_task is not thread-safe and call_soon_threadsafe cannot schedule coroutines directly; asyncio.create_task inside callback — rejected as asyncpg docs suggest callbacks may not always be on the event loop thread.

decision.choice: IndexQueue opens its own AsyncSession per event via _AsyncSessionFactory rather than accepting a db session parameter
decision.rationale: Queue items are processed asynchronously and long after the originating HTTP request session has closed. Each _process_event call therefore needs its own independent database session to avoid holding connections open across the full queue drain time.
decision.alternatives-considered: Passing a db session into process_queue — rejected: sessions are not safe to hold open across arbitrary async waits; using a dependency-injected session pool — rejected: over-engineered for a background task.
